about.headline: Change you can
about.lead: Less dependency. Better decisions. Software people actually use. Three changes I helped teams deliver.

identity.label: About Han Che
identity.name: Han Che
identity.body: I connect the commercial, technical and human sides of change. Engineer, team lead and trainer, with 2,000+ hours of coaching and training.

about.readingKey: Read each case: before → intervention → result
about.contactTitle: Where is the work getting stuck?
about.closing: Start with the people, the process and the tools. Not another tool in isolation.
about.provenance: Selected first-person accounts, cross-checked against my CV and professional profile. These describe my contribution within teams, not independently audited results.

rib.title: A team that doesn't wait for its manager.

before.title: One gatekeeper
before.caption: Every decision queued behind one person.
before.body: Refinement, estimates, assignments and reviews converged on one gatekeeper. The team had too little ownership to move independently.

intervention.title: Shared decisions
intervention.caption: Shared planning, capacity and peer review.
intervention.body: I coached shared refinement and estimation, made capacity explicit and built peer review. Team members took responsibility for planning and their own Scrum rituals.

result.title: Independent team
result.caption: The team ran its own Scrum in ~5 months.
result.body: In ~5 months, the team was running its own Scrum rituals with little need for me to be in the room. Distributed ownership became daily practice.

rib.scope: About five months of team development. “Runs itself” refers to day-to-day team routines, not an organisation without leadership.
rib.note: My intervention was not another approval layer. I helped the team refine and estimate together, communicate its capacity and unblock work with other teams. Peer review gave colleagues a way to build agreement and carry decisions themselves.
rib.source: Basis: personal accomplishment notes; Engineering Manager role and five-month transformation recorded in my CV.

audi.title: Less meeting. More deciding.
audi.unit: minutes saved per meeting, on average

before.title: Legacy approval
before.caption: Brief: rebuild the Excel approval flow.
before.body: The final approval before serial production depended on a legacy process. The starting request was to reproduce the existing Excel workflow.

intervention.title: Model the process
intervention.caption: Stakeholder sessions became a state model.
intervention.body: With an architect colleague, I worked through stakeholder sessions, state diagrams and a relational data model. We built one core process end to end.

result.title: Digital sign-off
result.caption: A core-process demo, meetings 30 min shorter.
result.body: The core-process demo made the model tangible. The digitisation effort also shortened approval meetings by an average of 30 minutes.

audi.scope: 6–8 weeks refers to the working core-process demo. The initial release took 6 months. The 30-minute figure is the average meeting reduction, not a demo benchmark.
audi.note: State transitions gave stakeholders a model in their own domain language. The demo ran on pre-production with data import and export, side by side with the existing tool. It was a concrete basis for agreement on how the process should work.
audi.source: Basis: personal accomplishment notes for the demo; CV for the six-month initial release and average meeting reduction.

selfbits.title: Beyond the demo. Into production.

before.title: Production data
before.caption: Orders needed to become usable OEE data.
before.body: How can production orders become usable data about equipment effectiveness? The work needed to connect manufacturing processes with the people operating them.

intervention.title: Build and pilot
intervention.caption: Web, mobile and TV software, built and run.
intervention.body: I designed, implemented and operated manufacturing execution software with the team: web, mobile and TV interfaces for scheduling, master data and OEE.

result.title: Software in use
result.caption: 200+ users, 3 HEPA lines piloted in 9 months.
result.body: The software served 200+ users across the total deployment. A defined pilot acquired order-based OEE data on 3 HEPA lines in 2 factories within 9 months.

selfbits.scope: 5 factories and 200+ users describe the total deployment in my CV. The nine-month milestone covers the 3-line, 2-factory pilot, not the full rollout.
selfbits.note: Manufacturing execution software connects production planning with work on the factory floor. OEE means overall equipment effectiveness. Here, the pilot concerned acquiring that data per production order; no percentage improvement in OEE is claimed.
selfbits.source: Basis: CV for deployment and pilot scope; professional profile for work on scheduling, OEE dashboards and master data.

ai-token-economy.title: The AI Token Economy
ai-token-economy.caption: AI can give you and the people you lead super powers, but it comes with hidden managing responsibilities you didn't sign up for.
ai-token-economy.description: A field guide to the token economy: what AI actually costs, why the meter stays invisible, and how to manage context and models efficiently.

motivation.title: Motivation
motivation.caption: Thought experiment: Imagine you're assigned a freelancer with these weird characteristics.
motivation.prose: On paper, this collaborator arrives with encyclopedic knowledge, works instantly, and accepts tasks without hesitation. But they carry three peculiar flaws.

freelancer-metaphor.description: Translates abstract LLM mechanics into intuitive human management terms: encyclopedic knowledge, instant execution, but crucial blind spots.

management-opt-in.description: Treating an LLM as a teammate requires recognizing its failure modes rather than treating it as an infallible search oracle.

lead-one-upskill-many.title: Lead One, Upskill Many
lead-one-upskill-many.caption: It's an LLM — but if it were a human, how would you manage it?
lead-one-upskill-many.prose: Directing an AI agent requires the same delegation and review rigor as onboarding an external specialist.

upskill-vs-replace.description: The objective is not replacing workers but elevating human operators into effective directors of synthetic labor.

the-four-eras-of-ai.title: The Four Eras of AI
the-four-eras-of-ai.caption: New technology gives rise to new disciplines for humans to cope.
the-four-eras-of-ai.prose: From Prompt Engineering in 2023 to Context Engineering in 2024, Harness Engineering in 2025, and Token Economics today.

emerging-disciplines.description: As model capabilities advance, operational focus shifts from prompt words to managing context, harnesses, and token budgets.

the-invisible-invoice.title: The Invisible Invoice
the-invisible-invoice.caption: For a real freelancer you need a business case. AI just bills you.
the-invisible-invoice.prose: A €3,200 consultant invoice requires purchase orders and approvals. AI accumulates identical costs silently across thousands of micro-prompts.

governance-asymmetry.description: Corporate finance demands formal approval for contractors, yet AI charges comparable budgets without procurement gates.

outcome-per-euro.title: Outcome Per Euro
outcome-per-euro.caption: You're now accountable for a budget you never signed up to manage.
outcome-per-euro.prose: Defaulting to flagship frontier models for routine chores burns capital. The economic winner optimizes outcome per euro.

budget-accountability.description: Selecting the right tier for each task is the foundation of modern engineering leadership.

what-is-a-token.title: What Is a Token
what-is-a-token.caption: Tokens are the basic unit of data for LLMs — every one is billed.
what-is-a-token.prose: LLMs calculate statistical probabilities over numerical tokens. Every word, character, and prompt translates to billable units.

probabilistic-units.description: LLMs process numerical token IDs, not human prose. Understanding token granularity reveals where costs accumulate.

live-context-breakdown.title: Live Context Breakdown
live-context-breakdown.caption: Most tools hide the meter — this is what seeing it looks like.
live-context-breakdown.prose: A typical 200k session breakdown: system prompts, conversation history, tool payloads, and retrieved documentation.

synthetic-abstractions.description: Commercial interfaces conceal real token usage behind credits and bars. Direct transparency is essential for optimization.

cli-vs-web-tool-obscurity.title: CLI vs Web Tool Obscurity
cli-vs-web-tool-obscurity.caption: The meter is hidden on purpose.
cli-vs-web-tool-obscurity.prose: Obscurity is a product pattern: frictionless initiation, habitual workflows, and surprising monthly invoices.

the-obscurity-playbook.description: Hiding usage metrics fosters dependency before organizations realize the compounding cost of unmanaged agentic loops.

managing-context.title: Managing Context
managing-context.caption: Context window is the model's attention span.
managing-context.prose: Tokens accumulate in the context window. As the window fills, attention degrades and critical instructions slip away.

cognitive-stamina.description: Context windows behave like cognitive stamina across a long workday: alert early on, distracted as history piles up.

the-lost-middle.title: The Lost Middle
the-lost-middle.caption: How key instructions get lost in the middle.
the-lost-middle.prose: Models attend sharply to the start and end of context, but the middle blurs into an attention valley.

attention-valley.description: Research proves the U-shaped retrieval curve: information placed in the middle of long contexts suffers dramatic recall drops.

the-fullness-gauge-and-levers.title: The Fullness Gauge & Levers
the-fullness-gauge-and-levers.caption: Past ~half full, the model starts losing the plot.
the-fullness-gauge-and-levers.prose: Below 50% is the smart zone. Above 50%, accuracy degrades. Above 75%, hallucination risk spikes. Three levers: Monitor, Compact, Hand off.

smart-zone-discipline.description: Keeping context windows under 50% capacity guarantees high accuracy and prevents silent prompt drift.

cost-of-agentic-ai.title: Cost of Agentic AI
cost-of-agentic-ai.caption: One small bug fix compounds to ~73,000 tokens of context.
cost-of-agentic-ai.prose: Agentic loops re-transmit the entire conversation history on every single tool call and reflection step.

agentic-compounding.description: Each tool call and test run appends full file outputs into history, compounding input token counts exponentially.

the-compounding-cost-curve.title: The Compounding Cost Curve
the-compounding-cost-curve.caption: The same bug fix, priced across models.
the-compounding-cost-curve.prose: You are billed for tokens processed on every turn, not window capacity. A routine bug fix produces a 14× price swing across models.

the-14x-spread.description: At scale, routing identical loops between frontier and economy tiers creates a multi-thousand-dollar difference each month.

model-tiers.title: Model Tiers
model-tiers.caption: My real model stack: one workflow, many models.
model-tiers.prose: Route each phase to the most economical capable model: flat-rate chats for ideation, frontier reasoning for architecture, fast models for code execution.

tiered-stack-architecture.description: Economic fluency means matching engine cost to task risk, switching models seamlessly as project phases progress.

zero-marginal-thinking.description: Use flat-rate consumer subscriptions for exploratory chats, reserving pay-per-token frontier calls for high-leverage decisions.

tools-and-tips.title: Tools & Tips
tools-and-tips.caption: Three levers to improve your token economy
tools-and-tips.prose: Combine automated tooling (rtk, compression, linting) with structural context steering and disciplined team habits (edit don't append, session hygiene).

tooling-and-steering.description: Automated compressors prune tool payloads before they reach the model, while structured rules steer execution deterministically.

operational-habits.description: Edit flawed prompts instead of stacking corrections, clear idle sessions before cache expiry, and monitor usage via transparent CLIs.
